findings.description: Tests use >= or > assertions where exact counts are needed
findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 4: BuiltArtifactIndex (integration) and BuiltOutputs (build-system tests) replace first-match find_map with unique-path lookup and exactly-one selectors; reachable-dependency test asserts the exact emitted path set plus the lowered dependency body and its call site; JS glue, runtime-module and canvas tests assert exactly-one glue/canvas/runtime artifacts at exact paths and that the page imports the module actually emitted; frontend pipeline tests assert exact function-origin multisets and side-table coverage instead of functions_analyzed >= N; borrow-checker pipeline test asserts statement/terminator fact sets equal the lowered statements/blocks and an exact snapshot count; source-package benchmark warning test asserts an exact warning multiset; HIR local lowering tests assert exact authored locals and exactly one assignment to the authored local

findings.description: Golden comparison accepts directory entries as empty golden files
findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 5: the golden comparison decides the artifact kind before reading content. A Directory or NotBuilt entry is a kind mismatch instead of empty bytes, text goldens require strict UTF-8 (invalid UTF-8 is a HarnessFailed, not a silent rewrite), and binary/wasm goldens compare bytes only. Phase 5 closeout: the expected artifact kind is owned by the authored golden's own extension (GoldenFile.expected_kind), so a cross-kind match is rejected before content is read and identical bytes emitted as a different artifact kind cannot satisfy the golden. Regressions cover directory-vs-empty-file, an unbuilt path, invalid UTF-8, binary byte comparison, a duplicate-path artifact set, a JS golden against generic bytes, a wasm golden against generic bytes, an HTML golden produced as JavaScript outside the universal index.html baseline path, and a binary golden that must still match generic bytes

findings.description: HTML/Wasm baseline tests rely on broad fragment matching
findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 5: the HTML shell contract is now ordered, bounded and unique (html_shell_violation, one owner shared with the HTML builder's own shell tests), and the HTML-Wasm baseline derives its required exports from the emitted page.js (instance.exports.<name>) and checks each against the module's typed export kind, with an explicit ABI floor including moth_start. Duplicate exports and imports are rejected, and the page script include must appear exactly once inside the body. Phase 5 closeout: the shell contract is structural rather than a raw substring count. Script and style content is opaque payload the shell inserts, so marker-like text such as a JavaScript string spelling '</body>' no longer counts as a second element, while a marker repeated in real markup is still rejected

findings.description: Node runtime harness tests can hang without timeout
findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 5: the harness owns a tempfile workspace whose removal failure is reported, runs Node under a 30s deadline with kill-and-reap, drains stdout/stderr on their own threads with a 4 MiB bound, decodes protocol output strictly, and parses only supported <script> shapes. Typed RenderHarnessError{kind,message} separates Artifact/Workspace/Spawn/Timeout/ExitStatus/OutputDecoding/OutputProtocol/ScriptShape/Cleanup. Phase 5 closeout: both capture threads are joined before any result is inspected so no failure path drops a live thread; termination always attempts the reap and reports the kill and wait outcomes separately; type="module" is rejected rather than executed under classic semantics because the harness materializes no glue, provider or runtime module and no import map; nameless or malformed attribute tokens fail closed instead of being skipped; and every failure class now has a focused self-test, including Artifact (missing and wrong-kind), Workspace (write collision) and Spawn (a nonexistent interpreter through the process owner's executable seam, not a PATH mutation)

findings.description: Timing/concurrency tests depend on machine speed

findings.description: Feature-gated test modules need explicit execution lane mapping
findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 8: eight package-scoped lanes in xtask feature_matrix, run by `just test-feature-matrix`, cover every declared feature. `just feature-lane-check` (part of `just validate`) reads Cargo.toml and every cfg attribute in src and xtask/src, and fails when a declared feature has no lane, when a lane names an undeclared feature, or when a cfg names a feature that does not exist; it writes target/test-reports/feature_lane_coverage.json. The check also exposed that the previous workspace-wide feature commands never ran the default configuration, because xtask depends on moth with features = ["timers"] and Cargo unifies features across one resolve graph

findings.description: Tests rely on filesystem timestamps
findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 6: write_project_outputs returns a typed OutputWriteSummary and the two skip-unchanged tests assert Written / SkippedUnchanged directly, so both 30ms sleeps and both modification-time comparisons are gone; the remaining timestamp reads are the dev-server watch fingerprints, whose tests set modification times explicitly

findings.description: The counters-only feature configuration compiles a test helper no caller can reach
findings.disposition: found in Phase 8 when the counters lane became an executed command; routed to Phase 11. frontend_counters::capture_frontend_counters_for_test, FrontendCounterTestCaptureGuard and the re-export are gated on benchmark_counters, while every caller is gated on all(timers, benchmark_counters), so the counters-only lane emits three dead-code warnings. Nothing fails. It was invisible because `just ci-clippy-native` lints with --all-features and never builds that configuration. The correction is a cfg gate, not a behaviour change, so it is left outside the Patch A evidence boundary

findings.description: CI steps are monolithic
findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 8: the validation workflow runs nine gates (clippy, unit-tests, feature-matrix, integration, docs, benchmarks, timers-erasure, source-audit, honesty-audit) as independent jobs on Linux, macOS and Windows with fail-fast disabled, so one failed family never stops another from reporting. Windows stays non-blocking through a job-level continue-on-error, and validation.mtf > Platform policy now states the two conditions that end that status. The integration, feature-matrix and honesty-audit gates upload target/test-reports/ whether they passed or failed. `just validate` keeps the fail-fast local ordering, and the release workflow deliberately keeps it too. validation.mtf also lost its claim that `just ci-clippy` lints Linux and Windows x64 targets: that recipe does not exist and never did the cross-target work

findings.description: Acceptance-only smoke cases overclaim coverage
findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 7: all 12 acceptance-only backend blocks (exactly the 12 smoke-role cases) promoted to rendered_output_exact runtime contracts with a manifest contract and a non-smoke role, and each fixture comment rewritten to state what the case proves; the suite now declares zero acceptance-only blocks and zero smoke roles. Acceptance-only and the smoke role remain legal; schema 7 of the suite inventory reports smoke_role_cases and per-backend weak_contract_reviews so a returning weak contract stays findable

findings.description: Any #[ignore] tests would lack governance

findings.description: Tests comparing source text create false confidence
findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 8: xtask source_audit is now the one owner of broad-source architecture bans. It walks src and xtask/src once, fails closed on unreadable paths, reports typed findings (timer-erasure, removed-legacy-conversion-name, removed-legacy-payload-variant, unreadable-source) and writes target/test-reports/source_audit.json. Three source-text tests were deleted into it: the diagnostics conversion-name tripwire, old_error_payload_has_been_removed_from_diagnostic_payloads (which read one file) and timer_facade_sources_never_use_cfg_timer_macro (which read four). The audit applies both removed-name bans across the whole tree rather than to the single file each test read. timers-erasure-check kept only its compiled-artifact half and now defines the timer rules that source_audit applies, so no second walk exists to skip a file silently. The remaining include_str! uses in src are CSS and JS assets that a test then parses or executes, which is input, not a source-text assertion

findings.description: Machine-readable reports can become stale or partial
findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 8: every report is written to a sibling temporary file, flushed and renamed into place, and a failed write removes the temporary file so the previous report survives instead of a partial new one. Each report carries a RunIdentity (run id, command, host OS and architecture, the features the binary was built with, runner thread count and completion state), and the inventory and triage reports are replaced by a completed:false report before the work starts, so an interrupted run leaves a report that says it did not finish. repository_commit became a typed repository_revision that distinguishes a discovered commit, a run outside a repository, and a failed discovery with its reason, instead of collapsing all three into null. Suite inventory schema 7 to 8; the triage report gained a schema version. Self-tests cover the started/completed transition observed from inside execution, the absence of a partial sibling, a blocked write leaving the previous report intact, and each revision classification

findings.description: frontend_benchmark_rejects_a_busy_raw_session_before_compilation failed once during Phase 5 validation and did not reproduce in 24 subsequent full-suite runs (including 6 at --test-threads=16)
findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 6: the flake reproduced on the Phase 6 baseline run and was the test's evidence, not the compiler. The outer-session 'every aggregate has zero samples' proxy is replaced by two deterministic ordering tests — a missing entry path must fail as TimingSession rather than PathValidation, and invalid source must fail as TimingSession rather than Compilation — neither of which depends on the process-global collector being quiet. The collector stays process-global because cross-thread recording is its production contract
